body_markdown:
## Quick Takeaways


-


Chinese enterprises expanding overseas face fragmented communication channels, strict compliance regimes, and data residency mandates across 180+ markets.


-


A programmable communication platform (CPaaS) eliminates the need to negotiate carrier-by-carrier in every country.


-


Twilio's global infrastructure — 335,000+ customers, 218+ voice-capable countries, 99.95% API SLA — provides a single integration point for SMS, voice, email, WhatsApp, and RCS worldwide.


-


Real-world results:[Uber](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/uber) operates Twilio-powered verification in 58 countries and 400+ cities;[Airbnb](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/airbnb) secures 60 million guests across 191 countries;[Domino's](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/dominos) achieved +700% ROI with Twilio Segment.


## The China-to-Global Moment


2026 marks a tipping point. According to public filings and industry reports, Chinese technology companies, DTC brands, and AI-native startups are expanding into Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Europe at an unprecedented pace. But going global isn't just about translating your app — it's about rebuilding trust with every new customer in every new market, at scale, in real time.


The challenge is deceptively complex: a verification SMS that takes 1.2 seconds to arrive in Shenzhen may take 45 seconds — or never arrive — in Lagos, São Paulo, or Jakarta if routed through the wrong aggregator. A customer support call that works perfectly on a Chinese carrier may hit IVR dead-ends on European networks. An email campaign that delivers at 99% in domestic markets may land in spam folders across North America if SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records aren't configured correctly.


This is the infrastructure gap that kills global ambitions.


## Why Carrier-by-Carrier Integration Doesn't Scale


Many Chinese enterprises begin their overseas expansion by signing direct agreements with local carriers in each target market. This approach seems cost-efficient at first, but the hidden costs compound quickly:


**Factor**


**Direct Carrier Approach**


**CPaaS Platform Approach**


**Integration time per market**


4–12 weeks


Hours (single API)


**Compliance management**


Manual per jurisdiction


Automated Trust Hub


**Failover & redundancy**


Self-built


Built-in (4-deep routing)


**Channel coverage**


SMS only (typically)


SMS, Voice, WhatsApp, RCS, Email


**Fraud protection**


None or basic


Fraud Guard (389M attacks blocked)


The math is straightforward: if you plan to operate in 20+ markets, the engineering cost of maintaining 20+ carrier integrations, each with its own API, SLA, compliance rules, and billing format, exceeds the cost of a unified CPaaS platform within the first year.


## What a Global Communication Stack Actually Looks Like


For Chinese brands going global, the modern communication stack has five layers:


### 1. Programmable Messaging (SMS, WhatsApp, RCS)


Twilio's Messaging APIs support SMS delivery to 180+ countries with a median delivery speed under 2 seconds. For markets where WhatsApp dominates (Brazil, India, Indonesia), the same API handles WhatsApp Business messages at $0.005/message. RCS — the next-generation SMS with rich media — is available at $0.0083/message for markets with Android dominance.


Scale proof:


-


[Klaviyo](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/klaviyo) sends approximately 10 billion messages per month through Twilio on behalf of its customers.


-


[THG](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/thg) processes 1 billion emails monthly, with Black Friday peaks hitting 3× daily volume.


### 2. Voice APIs for Global Customer Support


Twilio processes 34 billion calls annually across 218+ countries. For Chinese brands building overseas call centers, the Voice API supports inbound routing, outbound dialing, IVR workflows (via Studio's visual editor), warm/cold transfers, and PCI-compliant payment processing — all through a single integration.


**Case in point** :[Genspark](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/genspark) uses Twilio Voice API to make 800+ outbound calls daily with a 94.3% success rate, boosting user retention by 3.2×.


### 3. Email Delivery at Scale (SendGrid)


SendGrid has delivered over 7 trillion emails to date, with a current throughput of 205 billion+ emails per month. Deliverability sits at 99%, with a 99.99% uptime SLA and a median send-to-inbox speed of 1.9 seconds.


For Chinese e-commerce brands running promotional campaigns in Western markets, deliverability is the single most important metric.[eBay](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/ebay-2) sends over 1 billion emails per month through SendGrid.[Shopify](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/shopify-2) powers email for 1.7 million merchants with a 99.5% deliverability rate.


### 4. Identity Verification (Twilio Verify)


Account security is non-negotiable in global markets. Twilio Verify supports SMS OTP, Voice OTP, WhatsApp OTP, Email OTP, TOTP, Passkeys, and automatic RCS upgrade — across 200+ countries with a delivery rate exceeding 94%.


The pay-per-successful-verification model ($0.05/verification, failures free) is particularly attractive for Chinese brands watching unit economics carefully during expansion. Fraud Guard has blocked 389 million fraudulent verification attempts, saving customers $45 million.


**Global scale** :[Duolingo](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/duolingo) adds 100,000+ daily active users secured by Twilio Verify.[Endowus](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/endowus) achieves 96%–98% conversion rates on its verification flow.


### 5. Customer Data Platform (Twilio Segment)


The most overlooked layer. Chinese brands expanding to 10+ markets quickly face a data fragmentation crisis: user behavior data lives in separate analytics tools, CRM systems, ad platforms, and messaging channels across each market.


Twilio Segment unifies customer profiles across 450–700+ pre-built connectors, creating a single source of truth. It processed 12.1 trillion API calls in 2023 alone.


-


[ZALORA](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/zalora) doubled its conversion rate after deploying Segment.


-


[Domino's](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/dominos) achieved +700% ROI, reduced costs by 65%, and increased conversions by 23%.


-


[IBM](https://customers.twilio.com/en-us/ibm) uses Segment across 150 product lines.


## Compliance: The Silent Dealbreaker


Going global from China means navigating GDPR in Europe, TCPA in the U.S., LGPD in Brazil, and PDPA across Southeast Asia — simultaneously. Twilio provides:


-


**3-region data residency** (US, EU, AU) with GDPR-ready infrastructure


-


**Trust Hub** for centralized brand registration and KYC


-


**Privacy Portal** for data subject requests


-


**SPF, DKIM, DMARC, Link Branding, and Reverse DNS** for email authentication


-


**Voice Integrity and Interconnect** for call authentication


This compliance layer isn't optional — it's what separates brands that scale globally from brands that get blocked.


## Getting Started


Twilio's pricing philosophy — "Start for free. Then pay as you go" — removes the upfront investment barrier. No credit card is required to begin. SMS starts at $0.0083/message. SendGrid offers 100 free emails/day. Flex provides 5,000 free agent hours.


For Chinese enterprises evaluating CPaaS platforms for overseas expansion, the decision framework is simple: how many markets do you plan to enter, how fast, and how much engineering capacity can you afford to spend on infrastructure instead of product?


Twilio's answer: one API, 180+ countries, 335,000+ companies already running on it.
